title: Raft
summary:
Raft is [consensus](#/sd/f/consensus) with a **strong leader**. Time is cut into **terms**, numbered epochs (like "the 5th president"), and each term has at most one leader. A log entry is `(operation, term)` at an index.

**Election.** Followers expect heartbeats; when they stop, the first *randomized* timer to fire wins the race: it becomes a candidate, increments its term, votes for itself and asks for votes. A node grants a vote only if (1) the candidate's term is not behind its own, (2) it has not already voted in that term (**one vote per term**), and (3) the candidate's log is at least as up to date as its own (higher last log term, or same term and longer log). A majority wins. The **term is a [fencing token](#/sd/f/fencing-token)**: any node that sees a higher term updates it, and an old leader steps down.

**Replication.** The leader sends AppendEntries: a *prefix check* ("my previous entry is `(term, index)`") plus new entries. A follower whose log doesn't match rejects; the leader steps back and retries until the prefixes line up, then the follower takes the leader's suffix. An entry is **committed** once stored on a majority; the leader advances a **commit index** (sent along in later AppendEntries) and followers apply entries up to it. A leader counts replicas only for entries of its own term; committing one commits everything before it.

**Edge case:** if the leader dies mid-write, an uncommitted entry may later survive or vanish. The client saw no ack, so it must retry with an [idempotency key](#/sd/f/idempotency).

drills.q: A 5-node cluster has leader L in term 5. A partition isolates L with one follower; the other three elect a new leader in term 6 and commit entries. The partition heals and L sends a heartbeat with term 5. What happens?
options: L's message is rejected with term 6; L steps down to follower and its uncommitted entries are overwritten with the new leader's log
The followers accept L's heartbeat because it was leader first
Both leaders keep serving writes until an admin picks one
The new leader steps down because L has been leader longer
drills.explain: Terms act as fencing tokens: a message from a lower term is rejected, and the reply carries the higher term so the stale leader reverts. L could never have committed anything in the minority partition, so no committed data is lost.

drills.q: A follower in term 7 receives RequestVote(term 7, candidate C). Which conditions must hold for it to grant the vote? Select all that apply.
options: It has not already voted for another candidate in term 7
C's log is at least as up to date as the follower's log
C's term is not lower than the follower's current term
C has the lowest node id
drills.explain: One vote per term guarantees at most one winner per term; the log up-to-date check ensures the winner holds every committed entry; the term check rejects stale candidates. Node id plays no role in Raft (randomized timers break ties).

drills.q: A Raft cluster has 7 nodes. Including the leader, how many nodes must have stored an entry (of the leader's current term) before the leader can mark it committed?
drills.explain: A majority of 7 is floor(7/2) + 1 = 4, counting the leader's own copy. Three followers' acknowledgements are enough.

drills.q: Put a Raft leader election in order.
items: Heartbeats from the leader stop arriving
A follower's randomized election timer fires first
It increments its term, becomes a candidate and votes for itself
It sends RequestVote to the other nodes and a majority grants it
It becomes leader and sends AppendEntries to establish authority
drills.explain: Randomized timers make it unlikely that two followers start at once; if they do, votes split, nobody wins, and a later timer retries in a higher term.

drills.q: The leader's next entry is index 10 (previous entry: index 9, term 4). A follower's log ends at index 7. The leader sends AppendEntries with prefix (index 9, term 4) and entry 10. What happens?
options: The follower rejects it; the leader backs up for this follower (prefix at index 8, then 7, ...) until the prefixes match, then sends the whole missing suffix
The follower stores entry 10 and leaves a gap at 8 and 9
The follower starts a new election because it is behind
The leader declares the follower failed and removes it from the cluster
drills.explain: The prefix check is what keeps logs identical: an entry is only appended if the entry before it matches. The leader's retry backfills the missing entries while carrying the new write.

drills.q: A 5-node leader appends an entry to itself and one follower (2 of 5), then crashes. The client received no response. Which statements are true? Select all that apply.
options: The entry may be lost if a node without it wins the election
The entry may survive and be committed if a node that has it wins
The client cannot know which happened, so its retry must be safe to repeat
The entry is guaranteed to appear in the new leader's log
drills.explain: Only 2 nodes hold it, so a candidate lacking it can win the votes of the three that don't. Raft guarantees committed entries survive; an uncommitted entry has no such promise. Hence the idempotency key on retry.
